lines.text: Many learners say: I don't like it too.
Better: I don't like it either.
After don't, use either, not too.
Either! I don't like it either.

data.why: After don't, use either, not too.

native.tip: En español “tampoco”, pero en inglés “too” no va en frases negativas: usa “either” al final.

en.tip: Learners think of “tampoco”, but “too” does not work in negative sentences. Use “either.”
en.caption: Common mistake: “I don't like it too.” In negative sentences, “too” becomes “either”: “I don't like it either.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
